findings_and_reconnections.classification: A source-level public API membership weakness; earlier cross-table risk already observed. No independent unique finding count asserted.
relationships: Adler READ-L11-372 role2323 explicitly noted foreign table columns in the historical matrix
Original Lens12 delegate READ-L12-767 role2323 observed that a column from another table is not tied to a specific transform
059 q2410 and q2414 retain narrower owner/test-source qualifications; exact cross-family aliases remain open
findings_and_reconnections.trace: ModelParameterTable<T> and ModelParameterColumn are public reexports. push returns an ordinal; resize can shrink that same table; Index and IndexMut immediately use the stored ordinal as a Vec index. A column obtained from a table then retained after shrinking that table to zero is no longer a member. ModelParameterRow::get checks numeric length, but a same-index column obtained from a different transform can still select an unrelated coefficient because the ordinal carries no transform identity.
findings_and_reconnections.limits: These are representable public inputs and symbolic outcomes, not an observed caller, actual constructed fixture or runtime panic. Normal parse_parameter_sets resolves a name from the same transform and indexes a table allocated to that transform's count, so no ordinary-parser mismatch is established. Whether cross-instance misuse merits an owning view/API change requires caller and policy review.
findings_and_reconnections.future_repair: Provide checked table access for unproven/stale ordinals and an owning name/column iteration or equivalent source-aware selection where actual cross-transform association matters. Preserve normal insertion order and first-duplicate policy; do not impose unnecessary instance branding.

findings_and_reconnections.classification: Existing historical source finding reconnected to public current API and ordinary producer.
relationships: Existing current REVIEW-FBX-MHR-CYCLIC-JOINT-GRAPH-95E concerns a distinct malformed FBX source cycle
findings_and_reconnections.trace: The exported skel_state::prefix_multiplication_levels accepts a public RigJointTable<Option<RigJointOrdinal>>. With one element whose parent is ordinal zero, its ancestor walk repeatedly selects itself and appends to a Vec, with no cycle check. The ordinary SkeletonBuilder appends a parent before its children and, for a terminating visit, supplies prior ordinals; an arbitrary public table can bypass that producer.
findings_and_reconnections.limits: Static representable case only: no parent table was constructed or algorithm run. A cyclic FBX graph can fail earlier in recursive builder traversal and is a different route; duplicate graph identities and actual callers remain separately open.
findings_and_reconnections.future_repair: Admit acyclic parent relationships at the actual public topology boundary or make invalid topology unrepresentable, with bounded error handling. Preserve valid roots, branches and ordinal order.

findings_and_reconnections.classification: Rejected suspicion by source and mathematical reasoning; original delegate had already recorded same qualification.
relationships: Original READ-L12-768 delegate role2325 explicitly explained all intermediate depths of a tree exist
findings_and_reconnections.trace: For any finite acyclic parent forest with maximum depth D, every integer depth 0 through D appears along a maximum-depth chain. For each bit level l with 2^l <= D there is therefore a node at depth 2^l whose depth has bit l set; the collected source list cannot first become empty while a higher bit remains. When the bit is set, the selected ancestor index is between 0 and depth−1.
findings_and_reconnections.limits: Proof assumes finite acyclic, in-range parent topology; q433/q434 concern inputs that violate that premise. No implementation or simulation was executed.
findings_and_reconnections.future_repair: No fix for the first-empty break under these assumptions; preserve valid scan behavior when addressing topology admission.
